recipe.title: Honey Garlic
recipe.subtitle: Chicken Thighs
recipe.description: Skillet chicken thighs in a sweet, garlicky honey-soy sauce, topped with cilantro and great over rice.
recipe.note: Recipe by Eric VanLandingham, from Allrecipes (https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/282124/honey-garlic-chicken-thighs/). Cook's notes: You can use skin-on, skinless, boneless, or bone-in chicken thighs. If using bone-in thighs, allow about 5 to 10 minutes longer than the original cook time. You can use an entire medium head of garlic, chopped, instead of individual cloves. If serving over rice, plan on about 3 to 4 cups uncooked rice to serve alongside and soak up the extra sauce. Garnish with fresh parsley instead of cilantro if you like.

items: salt and ground black pepper to taste
2 tablespoons olive oil, or as needed
7 cloves garlic, chopped, or to taste
1 pinch onion powder, or to taste
1 pinch garlic powder, or to taste

steps.title: Gather
steps.text: Gather all ingredients.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Season chicken on both sides with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Brown
steps.text: Heat olive oil in a cast iron skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken and brown on one side, 3 to 5 minutes.

steps.title: Add aromatics
steps.text: Flip chicken and add onion and garlic; continue to cook until chicken is mostly (but not fully) cooked and onion and garlic are soft, 5 to 7 minutes more. Remove chicken to a plate.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Add honey, soy sauce, onion powder, and garlic powder to the skillet. Stir and scrape the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon to get garlic and onion to mix with the liquid.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Return chicken to the skillet, cover, and reduce heat to medium. Cook until no longer pink in the center and juices run clear, about 10 more minutes, turning once halfway through. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of a thigh should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Arrange chicken on a serving plate and drizzle liquid from the pan on top. Sprinkle with cilantro to serve. Enjoy!

recipe.title: Dewey’s House Salad
recipe.subtitle: Copycat with Balsamic Vinaigrette
recipe.description: Mixed greens with cranberries, goat cheese, toasted pine nuts, balsamic dressing, and optional chicken.
recipe.total: 1 hour 26 min, including minimum chicken marinade
recipe.note: Source: Alaina Hinkle, Honest Grub, Honest Foodie — https://www.honestgrubhonestfoodie.com/easy-copy-cat-deweys-house-salad/. No contributor changes. Chicken is optional. Total calculated from listed prep, cook, and minimum marinade; longer marinating increases total. The source’s nutrition excludes dressing.

items: 6 tbsp balsamic vinegar, more if needed
2 tsp monk fruit sweetener or cane sugar

steps.title: Blend dressing
steps.text: Blend all vinaigrette ingredients with an immersion blender until creamy. Store in an airtight dressing container.

steps.title: Marinate optional chicken
steps.text: Season both sides. In an 8 × 8-inch dish, coat chicken with 1/2 cup dressing. Cover; refrigerate 1–24 hours.

steps.title: Cook optional chicken
steps.text: Melt butter over medium heat until simmering. Add chicken with its coating; discard remaining marinade. Cover pan with foil; cook 7–8 minutes per side, depending on thickness. Rest on a plate.

steps.title: Toast pine nuts
steps.text: Spread nuts evenly in a skillet over medium heat. Stir frequently until golden, about 5 minutes; avoid burning. Cool in a bowl.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Divide greens, cranberries, and cheese among four bowls. Add nuts and dressing; top with sliced chicken if desired.

recipe.title: Gigi Hadid
recipe.subtitle: Pasta
recipe.description: Creamy, tomato-forward vodka sauce tossed with penne and Parmesan, adapted to be less spicy and kid-approved.
recipe.note: Vodka is optional, but highly encouraged! Recipe by Barbara Sauermann, from Allrecipes (https://www.allrecipes.com/gigi-hadid-pasta-recipe-11900468). Her version adapts the original Gigi Hadid pasta to be less spicy and more tomato-y; increase the red pepper flakes if you like heat. Garnish with chopped basil if you like. Cook's note: If you like a lot of sauce, use less pasta or double the sauce.

items: 1/2 cup pasta cooking water, or as needed
1/2 onion, diced or 1 large shallot, diced
1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes, or to taste
salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste

steps.title: Cook the pasta
steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add penne and cook according to package instructions until just al dente, about 9 minutes. Scoop out 1/2 cup pasta water and set aside. Drain pasta.

steps.title: Build the base
steps.text: Meanwhile, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat and cook onion until soft and translucent, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Stir in tomato paste and cook, stirring, until tomato paste starts to darken and is well combined with the onion, 2 to 3 minutes.

steps.title: Add cream and vodka
steps.text: Pour in heavy cream and vodka and cook, stirring, for 2 minutes until alcohol evaporates. Stir in red pepper flakes and cook, stirring, until well combined. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Stir in butter until melted. Add drained pasta and 1/4 cup pasta water. Add more pasta water depending on how thick you like the sauce. Stir in freshly grated Parmesan cheese, taste, and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Continue cooking for 1 to 2 minutes over low heat until well combined.
